key_insight: No single rubric currently evaluates all major dimensions of clinical reasoning in LLMs, so existing tools need to be combined into a multi-part assessment framework.
clinical_relevance: For clinical AI, the paper highlights that exam-style accuracy is not enough; robust evaluation must also test temporal synthesis, uncertainty, counterfactual reasoning, and faithfulness to patient records.
method: Narrative review spanning medical education rubrics, clinical LLM benchmarks since 2023, and general long-form generation evaluation methods.
Mapped six reasoning dimensions: problem representation, temporal synthesis, differential/management reasoning, counterfactual reasoning, calibrated uncertainty, and reasoning faithfulness.
Proposes combining tools with binary rubric items, separate completeness vs correctness scoring, and reliability reporting.
evidence_signal: The review synthesizes published instruments and benchmarks, but the abstract notes that faithfulness has only one identified clinical causal-ablation study and that several dimensions remain under-evaluated.
watch_item: This is a design rationale rather than a validated instrument, so proposed rubric combinations still need testing for reliability, safety weighting, and longitudinal free-text use.
paper_title: A rubric landscape for evaluating clinical reasoning in large language models: what exists, what is missing, and what needs to be combined
